newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwaiti firm wins Niger gold search deal.
newsitem.headline: Kuwaiti firm wins Niger gold search deal.

text.p: Kuwait's Berlant General Trading Establishment signed an agreement with Niger's government to search for gold in the West African state's Kossa site, the company said on Monday.
"We have signed an agreement to search for gold and other precious metals in an area of 1,875 square kilometres," said Khaled Bastaki, chairman of the firm.
"The duration of the exploration franchise is 30 years."
Bastaki said his firm, which will spend $3.5 million exploring the site, is currently negotiating a partnership with three Canadian firms for the site exploration.

The site is part of the Liptako Gourma region. Officials in the African state have said Canada's Etruscan Enterprises Ltd made a promising find in the Liptako area in 1995 and it hoped to pour Niger's first gold ingot within two years.
Bastaki, the sole owner of Berlant General Trading, said he was seeking another deal with Niger's government to explore another site with an area of 1,000 square kilometres.
Niger has signed several similar deals with international firms since 1995.
